The proportion of patients developing heart failure within the first year after an atrial fibrillation diagnosis varies across Danish regions and hospital units, with a general downward trend observed over recent years for most institutions [^src1]. In the most recent reporting period, [[regionshospitalet-goedstrup|Regionshospitalet Gødstrup]] recorded the highest proportion at 7.1%, followed by [[friklinikken-region-syddanmark-grindsted|Friklinikken Region Syddanmark Grindsted]] and [[regionshospitalet-randers|Regionshospitalet Randers]], both at 6.6% [^src1]. At the other end of the spectrum, [[hospitalsenhed-midt|Hospitalsenhed Midt]] reported the lowest rate among major hospital units at 4.8% [^src1]. [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] as a whole showed a slightly lower regional average (5.7%) compared to [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] (5.8%) [^src1].

When examining trends across the 2020/21, 2021/22, and current reporting periods, most hospitals demonstrate a consistent decline in post-atrial fibrillation heart failure rates. For instance, [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]] improved from 10.2% to 5.9%, and [[regionshospitalet-randers|Regionshospitalet Randers]] dropped from 9.7% to 6.6% [^src1]. However, [[friklinikken-region-syddanmark-grindsted|Friklinikken Region Syddanmark Grindsted]] represents a notable outlier, with its rate rising from 2.5% in 2020/21 to 6.6% in the current period [^src1]. 

Data anomalies and statistical outliers are also present in the dataset. [[samso-sundheds-og-akuthus|Samsø Sundheds og Akuthus]] reported a 0.0% rate, but this is based on a tiny denominator of just 7 patients, resulting in a massive confidence interval of 0.0% to 41.0% [^src1]. Additionally, [[regionshospitalet-goedstrup|Regionshospitalet Gødstrup]] lacks historical data for the previous two periods, preventing trend analysis for this specific unit [^src1].
